name: Seven Wonders and the Heirs That Outlived Them
description: Six of the ancient world's marvels are gone. Follow the lists, the lost giants and the buildings that took their place in the traveller's imagination.

checkpoints.name: The one that stayed
checkpoints.note: Long before any Greek wrote a list, Egyptian builders raised a pyramid and carved a sphinx that would outlast every empire around them. Of the traditional seven, only the pyramid still stands.

checkpoints.name: Six marvels of the Greek world
checkpoints.note: Greek travellers counted the wonders they could see: gardens in Babylon, a temple at Ephesus, Zeus at Olympia, a tomb in Caria, a bronze giant at Rhodes and a lighthouse at Alexandria. Alexander's conquests opened the route to many of them.

checkpoints.name: Rome and the heirs of Greece
checkpoints.note: Earthquakes and invaders began to claim the wonders, while Roman engineers built new ones in concrete, from the Colosseum to the Pantheon. Petra and Hagia Sophia show how far the list could stretch.

checkpoints.name: A wider world of wonders
checkpoints.note: Later generations drew up lists of their own that reached beyond the Mediterranean. Angkor Wat, Chichen Itza, Machu Picchu, the Great Wall and the Taj Mahal were all seen by outsiders only slowly.
